q: On a road divided into lanes by visible lines, where in your lane should you normally drive?
choices: Close to the left line
Close to the right line
In the centre of the lane
Over a line, so you are more visible
hint: Think about leaving the same room on both sides of your vehicle.
explain: When a road is divided into lanes by visible marking lines, drive in the centre of your lane.
quote: When a roadway has been divided into lanes by visible marking lines on the road surface, you should drive in the centre of your lane.

q: You are driving on a highway and your exit is coming up. When should you be in the proper lane for it?
choices: Well before you reach the exit
Right as you reach the exit
Once you are beside the exit ramp
After the exit sign is behind you
hint: Last-minute moves at exits are something the guide warns against.
explain: Plan ahead and get into the proper lane well before your exit, then signal well in advance.
quote: Plan ahead. Be in the proper lane well before you reach your exit.
topic: Exiting: signal, deceleration lane, missed exit

q: What is a blind spot?
choices: The area that your inside mirror shows through the back window
An area beside and a bit behind you that your mirrors do not show
The part of the road lit up by your low-beam headlights
The stretch of lane directly ahead of your vehicle
hint: It is an area you can only see by turning your head.
explain: Your mirrors do not show everything to your sides, or what is right beside and slightly behind you in the next lanes. Those areas are blind spots.
quote: They will not show you everything to the sides or what is right beside and slightly behind in the lanes next to you. These are blind spots.

q: Before changing lanes, what must you do in addition to checking your mirrors?
choices: Flash your headlights
Do a shoulder check
Sound your horn
Slow down well below the traffic speed
hint: Mirrors miss certain areas next to your vehicle.
explain: To account for blind spots, you must do shoulder checks as well as mirror checks before changing lanes.
quote: To account for blind spots, you must do shoulder checks in addition to mirror checks before changing lanes.
topic: Lane change procedure (mirror, signal, shoulder check)

q: How do you do a proper shoulder check?
choices: Turn your whole body and look out the back window for a few seconds
Quickly glance over your shoulder through the rear side window, toward where you will move
Look over the shoulder on the side opposite to where you plan to move
Look in your inside rear view mirror for a few seconds
hint: Keep it short so your eyes are not off the road ahead for long.
explain: Quickly glance back over your shoulder through the rear side windows in the direction you intend to move. This shows the area your mirrors cannot.
quote: To shoulder check properly, quickly glance back over your shoulder through the rear side windows in the direction you intend to move.

q: Which order does the guide give for changing lanes?
choices: Signal, change lanes, then check your mirrors
Check mirrors, shoulder check, signal, then change lanes
Shoulder check, change lanes, then signal
Change lanes, signal, then shoulder check
hint: Checking comes before anything else.
explain: Make sure a lane change is permitted, check your mirrors, shoulder check, turn on your signal, change lanes if safe while keeping your speed, then turn off your signal.
quote: Check for traffic by glancing in your inside and outside rear view mirrors. Check over your shoulder to be sure there are no vehicles or cyclists in your blind spots. Turn on the proper signal light. If safe, change lanes while maintaining your speed as much as possible.
topic: Lane change procedure (mirror, signal, shoulder check)

q: On a multi-lane highway, which lane should slower traffic use?
choices: The lane furthest to the left
The lane furthest to the right
Any lane, as long as it is under the speed limit
The centre lane only
hint: One lane needs to be kept open for something.
explain: Slower traffic should use the travel lane furthest to the right (unless turning left), which leaves the left lane free for passing.
quote: On a multi-lane highway, slower traffic should use the travel lane furthest to the right (unless needing the left lane to turn left). This leaves the left lane available for other drivers to use for passing.
topic: Passing/climbing lanes; keep right except to pass

q: You are driving slowly on a highway when a passing lane begins. What should you do?
choices: Stay in the left lane and speed up
Move into the right lane so others can pass on the left
Pull onto the shoulder so others can get by
Stop until the passing lane ends
hint: The added lane is there so faster vehicles can get around you safely.
explain: Where there is a passing lane, slower vehicles move into the right lane so other vehicles can pass safely in the left lane.
quote: Slower vehicles move into the passing lane to the right, permitting other vehicles to pass safely in the left lane.
topic: Passing/climbing lanes; keep right except to pass

q: A passing lane is about to end. What does the guide say drivers should do?
choices: Right-lane drivers merge left, and left-lane drivers help them in
Left-lane drivers merge right, and right-lane drivers help them in
Right-lane drivers stop and wait for a clear gap
Left-lane drivers have the right-of-way and should speed up
hint: Think about which lane was the extra one added to the highway.
explain: Drivers in the right lane must merge safely with traffic to the left, and drivers in the left lane must cooperate to let them merge.
quote: When approaching the end of the passing lane, drivers in the right lane must merge safely with traffic to the left. Drivers in the left lane must cooperate to let drivers from the right lane merge.
topic: Passing/climbing lanes; keep right except to pass

q: You plan to pass a vehicle on a two-lane highway. Why should you do a shoulder check to the left first?
choices: To look for oncoming vehicles far ahead
To look for vehicles that may already be passing you
To check how fast the vehicle ahead is going
To check that the shoulder is clear to use
hint: You may not be the only driver who wants to pass.
explain: A vehicle may already be passing you on the left and could be hidden in your blind spot, so shoulder check left before you pull out.
quote: Do a shoulder check to the left to look for vehicles that may be passing you on the left. These vehicles may be in your blind spot.

q: While passing another vehicle, may you go over the speed limit?
choices: Yes, by up to 10 km/h
Yes, if the pass would take too long otherwise
No, it is illegal to exceed the speed limit when passing
Yes, but only on a two-lane highway
hint: Think about whether passing ever changes the posted limit.
explain: It is illegal to exceed the speed limit when passing another vehicle. If you have any doubts about completing the pass safely, do not attempt it.
quote: It is illegal to exceed the speed limit when passing another vehicle.
topic: No exceeding speed limit while passing

q: After passing a vehicle on a two-lane highway, when should you begin returning to your lane?
choices: As soon as your rear bumper has just cleared its front bumper
When you can see it in your inside mirror and a right shoulder check is clear
When the other driver flashes their headlights at you to come over
When you are about one car length ahead of the vehicle you passed
hint: One of your mirrors tells you when there is enough room.
explain: Once the passed vehicle is visible in your inside rear view mirror, shoulder check right, signal right, and return to your lane while keeping your speed.
quote: Once the vehicle you have passed is visible in your inside rear view mirror, do a shoulder check to the right. Turn on your right signal light. Return to your original lane while maintaining your speed.
topic: Passing: return when visible in mirror

q: Another vehicle is passing you on a two-lane highway. How can you help?
choices: Move to the left side of your lane
Stay in your lane and move to the right side of it
Stay exactly in the centre of your lane
Pull onto the shoulder to let it by
hint: Give the passing driver the best possible view of the road ahead.
explain: Stay in your lane and move to the right side of it. This gives the passing driver a better view of the road ahead.
quote: When being passed on a two-lane highway, help the driver passing you by staying in your lane. Move to the right side of your lane to give the other driver a better view of the road ahead.

q: You are on a two-lane highway outside any city or town. There is a solid yellow line on your side of the centre line and a broken yellow line on the other side. May you pass?
choices: Yes, because there is a broken line on the other side
No, because the solid yellow line is on your side
Yes, if no oncoming traffic is in sight
Yes, if you stay under the speed limit
hint: Think about which of the two lines is meant for drivers going your way.
explain: Do not pass when a solid yellow line is on your side of the centre line. The broken line only permits passing for drivers on the other side.
quote: a solid yellow line is on your side of the centre line

q: In which of these situations is it illegal to pass?
choices: The vehicle ahead stopped to let a pedestrian cross at a crosswalk
You are in the left lane of a multi-lane highway
You are using a marked passing lane on a highway
A broken line is on your side and no traffic is coming
hint: Think about what a stopped vehicle could be hiding from your view.
explain: Do not pass another vehicle that has stopped to let a pedestrian cross at a marked or unmarked crosswalk. The other choices describe places where passing is allowed.
quote: another vehicle is stopped to allow a pedestrian to cross at a marked or unmarked crosswalk

q: You are driving through a playground zone during its posted times, behind a slow car. May you pass it?
choices: Yes, if no children are visible
No, passing is illegal in the zone during those times
Yes, if the other driver waves you by
Yes, if the centre line is broken
hint: These zones have special rules while they are in effect.
explain: Do not pass in a school or playground zone during school or playground zone times.
quote: you are in a school or playground zone during school or playground zone times

q: A school bus ahead of you has stopped with its red lights flashing and its stop arm out. May you pass it?
choices: Yes, if you go slowly
Yes, if no children are visible
No, passing it is illegal
Yes, if you sound your horn first
hint: The stop arm means exactly what it looks like.
explain: Do not pass a school bus that has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended. These show that the bus has stopped.
quote: a school bus has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended indicating the school bus has stopped.
topic: School bus with flashing red lights / stop arm

q: A school bus ahead has flashing amber lights. What do these lights tell you?
choices: The bus has stopped and its stop arm is out
The bus is slowing and may be about to stop
The bus is leaving the stop and speeding up
The bus is empty and out of service
hint: Amber is a warning that comes before red.
explain: Flashing amber lights mean the bus is reducing speed and may be stopping to let passengers on or off. Passing it is not the safest choice; if you do, use caution.
quote: It is not the safest choice to pass a school bus that has flashing amber lights, indicating that it is reducing speed, because it may be stopping to allow passengers on and off the school bus.
topic: School bus with flashing amber lights: prepare to stop

q: You are driving up a hill on a two-lane highway. What should you do as you approach the top?
choices: Move to the right in your lane and do not pass
Move to the left in your lane to see over the top
Speed up and pass before you reach the top
Move closer to the centre line and keep going
hint: Someone coming the other way could be over the centre line, and you cannot see past the crest.
explain: Move to the right in your lane near the top of a hill in case an oncoming vehicle has crossed the centre line. Do not pass near the top of a hill, because you cannot see what is ahead.
quote: Use caution and move to the right in your lane as you approach the top of a hill. This may keep you from being hit by an oncoming vehicle that has crossed over the centre line and is in your lane. Do not pass near the top of a hill on a two-lane highway, as you cannot see what is ahead of you.
topic: Hills: approaching hilltop (keep right, no passing)

q: On a highway with one lane in each direction, may you pass another vehicle on a curve?
choices: Yes, if you stay under the speed limit
Yes, if you can see partway around the curve
No, it is unsafe and illegal
Yes, but only during daylight
hint: Think about how far ahead you can actually see on a bend.
explain: Do not pass vehicles on curves on highways with one lane in each direction. It is unsafe and illegal.
quote: Do not pass vehicles on curves on highways with one lane in each direction. It is unsafe and illegal.

q: What is the emergency stopping lane (the shoulder) of a primary highway for?
choices: Passing slower vehicles on the right
Pulling over so faster vehicles can pass you
Stopping because of an urgent situation or a vehicle problem
Driving slowly while you look for your exit
hint: The name of the lane tells you a lot.
explain: The emergency stopping lane is for drivers who need to stop because of an urgent situation or problems with their vehicle. Do not drive or pass in it.
quote: sometimes referred to as the shoulder, is for drivers who need to stop due to an urgent situation or because they have problems with their vehicle.

q: A driver behind you wants to pass. May you move onto the emergency stopping lane to let them by?
choices: Yes, if you signal first
Yes, if traffic is light
No, you must not use it to help another vehicle pass
Yes, but only on a two-lane highway
hint: That lane is kept clear for one purpose only.
explain: Do not drive in the emergency stopping lane, and do not pass or help another vehicle pass you by using it.
quote: Do not drive in the emergency stopping lane of a highway. Do not pass or assist another vehicle to pass you by using this lane.

q: You are merging onto a highway from an acceleration lane. Who has the right-of-way?
choices: You do, because you are merging
The vehicles already on the highway
Neither; merging is a shared responsibility
Whichever vehicle is larger
hint: Think about what happens if each driver expects the other to give way.
explain: Neither the merging vehicle nor the vehicles already on the highway have the right-of-way. Both must cooperate so the merge happens safely.
quote: Neither the merging vehicle nor the vehicles already on the highway have the right-of-way. Merging is a shared responsibility between the vehicles joining the roadway and the vehicles already on the roadway.

q: In the acceleration lane, what speed should you try to reach before merging?
choices: A slow speed, so you can stop at the end of the lane
The speed of the traffic on the main road
About half the speed of the highway traffic
Well above the speed of the highway traffic
hint: You want to blend in, not stand out.
explain: Accelerate to the speed of the traffic on the main road. Merging lanes are designed to let you reach the posted speed limit of the road you are joining.
quote: Merging lanes are designed to allow your vehicle to reach the posted speed limit of the road you are merging onto. ... Accelerate to the speed of the traffic on the main road.

q: Why should you avoid stopping or slowing sharply in an acceleration lane?
choices: Drivers behind you expect you to keep moving and could hit you
Highway traffic would then be required to stop and let you in
Stopping first gives you the right-of-way over highway traffic
Only large trucks are allowed to stop in an acceleration lane
hint: Think about who is following you down the ramp.
explain: The drivers behind you expect you to keep moving ahead. If you slow or stop, your vehicle may be hit from behind.
quote: The drivers behind you are expecting you to continue moving ahead. If you slow or stop your vehicle may be hit from behind.

q: When should you turn on your signal to merge onto a highway?
choices: Before or when you are in the acceleration lane
Only after you are on the highway
Only once you are past the solid white line
You do not need to signal from an acceleration lane
hint: Other drivers need time to see what you plan to do.
explain: Use your signal light before or when you are in the acceleration lane, and turn it off once you have merged.
quote: Use your signal light before or when you are in the acceleration lane.

q: When may you move from the acceleration lane into the highway lane?
choices: When it is safe and legal, after you are past the solid white line
As soon as you can, even across the solid white line
Only after coming to a full stop at the end of the lane
At the very end of the lane, whether or not there is a gap
hint: A line marking beside the acceleration lane tells you where the move becomes legal.
explain: Move into your chosen gap only when it is safe and legal, after you are past the solid white line of the acceleration lane.
quote: When it is safe and legal, move into the gap after you are past the solid white line of the acceleration lane.

q: You are in the right lane of a highway and vehicles are merging from an on-ramp. What should you do if it is safe?
choices: Speed up to close the gap
Move left to the next lane
Move onto the shoulder to make room
Stay right beside the merging vehicle
hint: Think about how to leave room for the vehicles joining the highway.
explain: If it is safe, move left to the next lane. This leaves the right lane clear for merging vehicles.
quote: If you are on the main roadway, and traffic is merging, move left to the next lane if it is safe. This leaves the right travel lane clear for the merging vehicles to enter.

q: When you exit a highway, where should you do most of your slowing down, if possible?
choices: In the deceleration lane
In the left lane before the exit
On the shoulder before the exit
In your highway lane, well before the exit
hint: Think about where slowing down will least affect the traffic behind you.
explain: Move into the deceleration lane if there is one and, if possible, do most of your slowing there. If it is short, you may need to start slowing on the highway.
quote: Move into the deceleration lane if there is one. If possible, do most of the slowing in the deceleration lane.
topic: Exiting: signal, deceleration lane, missed exit

q: You miss your exit on a freeway. What should you do?
choices: Stop on the shoulder and reverse back to the exit
Continue to the next exit and plan a way back
Stop in your lane until it is clear to reverse
Cut across at the last moment to make the exit
hint: A missed exit costs you a few minutes, not your safety.
explain: If you miss your exit, do not stop. Continue to the next exit and plan your return. Never stop and reverse on a highway, emergency stopping lane, or shoulder.
quote: If you miss your exit, do not stop. Continue to the next exit and make plans to return to your route. Do not stop and reverse on a highway, emergency stopping lane, or shoulder.
topic: Exiting: signal, deceleration lane, missed exit

q: When should you turn on your signal to exit a highway?
choices: Well in advance of the exit
Only once you are in the deceleration lane
After you have left the highway
You do not need to signal to exit
hint: Drivers behind you need time to adjust.
explain: Use your turn signal well in advance of the exit to alert other drivers, and turn it off once you have exited.
quote: Use your turn signal well in advance of the exit to alert other drivers.
topic: Exiting: signal, deceleration lane, missed exit

q: What is a weave zone?
choices: An area where the highway entrance and exit use the same lane
A stretch of highway with many sharp curves
A lane reserved for buses and car pools
The place where a passing lane ends
hint: Think about interchanges where an on-ramp and an off-ramp are very close together.
explain: A weave zone is where a highway entrance and exit share the same lane, so entering and exiting vehicles cross paths. Control your speed and the timing of your lane change.
quote: On some roadway interchanges, there are places where the highway entrance and exit use the same lane. ... The area that these vehicles share is called a weave zone.

q: If you need to slow down for a curve, when should you do it?
choices: Before you enter the curve
In the middle of the curve
As you leave the curve
By braking hard while turning
hint: Think about getting your speed set before the road starts to bend.
explain: Reduce your speed before entering the curve, stay centred in your lane, and keep a safe, steady speed through it.
quote: If you need to reduce your speed, do it before entering the curve, and stay centred in your lane.

q: Your vehicle starts to skid in a curve. What should you do?
choices: Brake hard and turn the steering wheel sharply the other way
Stay off the brake and gas, look where you want to go, and steer gently
Press the gas firmly to get the tires to grip the road again
Keep your eyes on the side of the road you are sliding toward
hint: Your eyes guide your hands.
explain: If you skid in a curve, stay off the brake and the accelerator. Keep looking where you want to go and make small steering adjustments.
quote: If you skid in a curve, stay off the brake and the accelerator. Continue to look in the direction you want to go, and make small steering adjustments to come out of the skid.

q: How does driving down a steep hill affect the time it takes you to stop?
choices: It takes longer to stop
It takes less time to stop
It makes no difference
It only matters on wet roads
hint: Think about which way the hill is pushing your vehicle.
explain: The time it takes to stop increases when travelling down a hill, so adjust your speed on very steep hills.
quote: If the hill is very steep, adjust your speed. The time it takes you to stop will increase when travelling down a hill.
topic: Hills: gear and speed on downgrades

q: In a vehicle with a standard transmission, what can you do going down a hill to reduce the risk of your brakes overheating?
choices: Shift to a lower gear
Shift to neutral and coast
Hold the clutch pedal down
Shift to a higher gear
hint: The engine can help hold the vehicle back.
explain: In a standard transmission vehicle, shifting to a lower gear can reduce the risk of your brakes overheating on a downhill.
quote: In a vehicle with a standard transmission, shifting to a lower gear can reduce the risk of your brakes overheating.
topic: Hills: gear and speed on downgrades
